title: How Much Do Contractor Leads Cost? (2026, by Channel)
h1: How Much Do Contractor Leads Really Cost? (2026)
meta: Contractor lead costs by channel, measured per BOOKED job: Google LSA ~$168, Thumbtack ~$250, Angi ~$542. Why per-lead pricing hides the real number.
short: Per booked job — the only number that matters — contractor leads run roughly $168 (Google LSA), $250 (Thumbtack), and $542 (Angi). Per-lead sticker prices ($25–$120) look cheaper but hide your close rate, which is where the real cost lives.
statLabel: Cost per booked job by channel (Google LSA → Angi), close rates included

body.answer: Measure per booked job, not per lead.
body.html: Per booked job, contractor leads run about $168 via Google LSA, ~$250 via Thumbtack, and ~$542 via Angi. Per-lead prices ($25–$120 depending on trade and metro) look cheaper, but they ignore the close rate — and on shared leads sold to up to 12 pros, that close rate is brutal.

body.answer: A cheap lead with a low close rate is an expensive job.
body.html: A '$35 lead' you win one time in twelve is a few hundred dollars per booked job. Take the lead price, divide by your close rate on that source, and compare channels on equal footing. That's when a 'cheap' shared lead reveals itself as the most expensive customer you can buy.

A complete Google Business Profile with steady reviews, a referral system, and a converting website generate exclusive leads at a fraction of the per-booked-job cost of any platform — and they don't disappear when you stop paying. Answer fast (5 min = up to 100x more likely to connect — MIT Sloan 2026) and they close.

faq.q: How much does a contractor lead cost in 2026?
faq.a: Per lead, $25–$120 depending on trade and metro. Per BOOKED job — the number that matters — roughly $168 (Google LSA), $250 (Thumbtack), $542 (Angi).

faq.q: Why is cost per booked job higher than cost per lead?
faq.a: Because it includes your close rate. On shared leads sold to up to 12 pros, most don't close, so the true cost per booked job is far above the per-lead price.

faq.q: What's the cheapest way to get contractor leads?
faq.a: Owned channels — Google Business Profile, referrals, and a converting website. Exclusive leads, lowest cost per booked job, and they compound over time.
